claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is a largely homogeneous solid solution without significant nanoscale phase separation.
A suitable post-deposition thermal treatment will drive Cu segregation in FeNiCrCoCu without degrading coating integrity.
The thermal treatment will form and refine nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates.
The Cu-rich precipitates may occur along grain boundaries or within the coating matrix.
Fine, dispersed precipitates provide an additional high-temperature strengthening mechanism.
Cu-rich precipitates strengthen the coating through Orowan-type dislocation pinning.
Cu-rich precipitates improve load sharing or load transfer during sliding.
The Cu-rich precipitates impede dislocation motion during high-temperature sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion limits localized microscopic plastic deformation.
Reduced localized plastic deformation enhances the overall sliding-wear resistance of the coating.
The precipitate-containing coating will have lower wear volume than the untreated homogeneous coating.
The precipitate-containing coating will have shallower wear scars than the untreated coating.
The precipitate-containing coating will exhibit a lower density of mobile dislocations after sliding.
The predicted wear and deformation benefits should hold at 600–700 °C under moderate contact stresses.
At substantially higher temperatures or in severe oxidative environments, oxidation or creep may obscure the precipitation-mediated wear mechanism.
The precipitate volume fraction, size, and spatial distribution needed to optimize wear resistance have not been quantified.
